Fortune Precision review: factory economics and funding constrain the growth outlook

Posted Oct 23, 2026, 8:38 a.m. EDT

Fortune Precision’s opportunity comes from supplying more qualified components to China’s semiconductor-equipment industry. The key test is how much accepted demand becomes recurring profit after materials, staffing, depreciation, research and the cash needed for expansion.

Our updated model estimates FY2027 revenue of approximately CNY6 billion and a Q4 2027 valuation of CNY39 per share. The valuation uses 20 times modeled recurring parent operating profit from Q4 2027 through Q3 2028. These are research estimates. Qualified capacity, product mix, collections and financing remain important uncertainties.

The proposed 65% RiYang purchase adds a small audited operating business at a cash price of approximately CNY189 million. Our forecast pays for integration, purchase-price amortization and the 35% minority interest. Shareholders approved the transaction on October 14; closing and payment have not been independently verified.

H1 2026 remains the latest reported period reviewed: revenue was CNY2,318 million, with a 27% gross margin. The issuer has scheduled Q3 results for October 28 and a management text briefing for October 29. Factory utilization, accepted advanced-component orders, working-capital conversion and funding terms are the next important checks.

Sources: H1 2026 issuer report, RiYang acquisition terms.

Western Digital pricing strengthens; research profit forecast rises

Posted Oct 23, 2026, 8:38 a.m. EDT

October 22, 2026 - Earnings and research model update

Western Digital reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $4.381 billion and adjusted operating profit of $2.153 billion. It expects December-quarter revenue of $5.0-5.2 billion, adjusted gross margin of 60-61% and adjusted operating expense of $400-410 million.

Our research model now estimates calendar 2027 revenue of $24.59 billion, up from $22.93 billion, and adjusted operating profit of $13.83 billion, up from $12.37 billion. These are research estimates, not company guidance.

Our Q4 2027 model valuation rises 6.2%, from $819 to $870 per share, using the same 20x adjusted operating-profit multiple and share convention. The calculation uses modeled profit over Q4 2027 through Q3 2028. This is a revision to a valuation estimate, not a share-price return.

Stronger producer pricing drives the change. The company shipped 223 nearline exabytes and 25 non-nearline exabytes. The prior forecast already included 223 nearline exabytes; the updated estimate therefore emphasizes price realization and higher-capacity mix rather than assuming the entire reported 248 exabytes was additional cloud volume.

The forecast also pays for more complex head and media production, component costs, warranty, qualification, staff, capital spending and depreciation. Earlier spot-price assumptions are replaced within the same storage market, avoiding a second revenue uplift from the same scarcity evidence.

Higher-capacity ePMR drives and 2027 HAMR qualifications remain important checkpoints. Customer planning visibility is stronger than before, but distant volumes and prices have less contractual coverage. High-bandwidth samples and the 55TB roadmap remain future opportunities, with no separate revenue assigned today.

The nearer Q4 2026 estimate rises 5% to USD 115; the Q1 2030 estimate rises 3% to USD 259. Each uses its own four-quarter profit window. Latest reported results cover Q2, released August 11. Lam and Meta: stronger demand, different earnings outcomes

Posted Oct 22, 2026, 8:40 a.m. EDT

October 21, 2026. Lam Research ($LRCX) and Meta Platforms ($META) reported quarterly results that show continued demand for advanced chips and AI services. Our updated forecasts reach different conclusions about the profits shareholders may capture.

Lam: a measured upgrade. Lam reported about $8 billion in quarterly revenue and expects about $9 billion next quarter. Management's preliminary outlook puts 2027 wafer-fabrication equipment spending above $200 billion. Management presentation, page 5. More complex memory and logic chips can increase demand for Lam's etch and deposition tools, while its installed equipment supports service and upgrade sales. Lam's results.

Our Q4 2027 profit-based ceiling rises from $321 to $331, up 3%. The earlier forecast already assumed a strong investment cycle. The revision accounts for that overlap, customer acceptance timing, manufacturing and support costs, and a more measured service forecast. These are research estimates rather than company share-price guidance.

Meta: advertising grows, infrastructure costs matter. Meta reported about $65 billion in quarterly revenue and expects $73–76 billion next quarter. Its advertising network offers a direct way to monetize better recommendations and AI tools. Personal agents could add subscriptions and commerce receipts, but early setups and activity do not establish paid revenue. Meta's results.

Our comparable Q4 2027 ceiling falls from $960 to $800, down 17%. The rebuilt forecast explicitly includes depreciation as data centers enter service, continuing operating costs and compensation. Meta has supplied no numerical 2027 consolidated revenue, expense or capex outlook. This reduction reflects our cost assumptions and risk assessment.

A separate New Mexico court judgment awards $25 billion plus 15% annual interest. Appeal outcomes, expense recognition and payment timing remain uncertain. This exposure is separate from the youth-settlement charge already included in Q3 earnings. Our scenarios test legal cash needs and uncommitted funding rather than assuming financing is free. Court judgment, page 20.

The Meta ceiling retains the previous economic share claim. After the intended pro-rata Class C distribution, the comparable claim would be an existing Class A share plus its distributed C share. The charter amendment is scheduled to take effect in January 2027; record and payment dates remain to be announced. New outside financing could dilute shareholder value. The distribution alone raises no cash.

Both ceilings use the same Q4 2027 through Q3 2028 earnings window and existing 20x operating-profit valuation methods. Lam uses company non-GAAP operating profit; Meta uses consolidated GAAP operating profit. Execution, monetization, legal outcomes and funding terms can change these estimates.

  • Alphabet ($GOOGL): our modeled value falls about 13% to $363 per share, from $415. The forecast separates Cloud services from hardware transferred to customers, then pays the manufacturing, support and infrastructure costs of each. More complete depreciation and rented-capacity costs reduce modeled operating profit. New AI software can improve returns, but its contribution depends on paid adoption after additional computing and support expense. Customer acceptance, competitive pricing and future funding remain uncertain. Alphabet second-quarter results

The established valuation multiples remain unchanged: 18x operating profit for Hammond Power and 20x for Amazon and Alphabet. These are research estimates, and execution, financing and costs can produce different outcomes.

Construction, accepted customer output and the amount of equipment brought into service remain important uncertainties. Amkor Arizona expansion

ASTRA Research

SpaceX raises the stakes for AI infrastructure

Posted Oct 21, 2026, 10:36 a.m. EDT

October 20, 2026

SpaceX reported about $15 billion of third-quarter revenue, including about $8 billion from its Superintelligence business. Management forecasts $33–37 billion of company revenue for the first quarter of 2027.

The biggest change is the pace of the proposed compute buildout. Management expressed high confidence in adding about 10 gigawatts during 2027, taking total capacity to about 13 gigawatts. Larger power plans still depend on construction, equipment, commissioning and financing.

Elon Musk also described a possible $500 billion–$1 trillion annualized revenue rate at the end of 2027 while discussing enterprise AI agents. That is an ambition rather than formal guidance. An annualized exit rate measures the pace reached near year-end; it does not mean the company collects that amount during 2027.

Our updated research model raises its Q4 2027 modeled value from about $100 to $296 per share, an increase of about 197%. It retains the same earnings multiple and includes depreciation, operating expenses and conditional share issuance. Delayed construction, the management capacity plan and a small-probability stretch outcome have separate revenue, cost and financing paths. These are research estimates, not company forecasts.

The distinction between cash generation and accounting earnings matters. Superintelligence produced about $5 billion of adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, while reported operating profit was about $400 million. Depreciation and employee share awards explain much of the difference. The company also expects $35–40 billion of capital spending in the fourth quarter. Further acquisition-accounting details remain pending.

For chip, memory, networking and power suppliers, the call supports a stronger demand outlook. Profit capture depends on qualified output, customer allocations, delivery dates and contract prices. Existing forecasts already assume substantial AI growth, so the same spending cannot be counted again for every supplier. SpaceX's internal turbine work also creates a competitive question for external power suppliers; it does not establish a canceled supplier order.

Sources: SpaceX Q3 results, investor relations and call replay.

Ouster forecast weighs stronger sensing competition and nearer-term cost guidance

Posted Oct 21, 2026, 10:36 a.m. EDT

October 20, 2026

Ouster faces a growing range of lidar and traffic-sensing alternatives. MicroVision announced a traffic-infrastructure alliance with Blue-Band on October 19, while other suppliers have reported commercial robotics shipments and named sensor selections.

Our updated model assigns a 30% probability to competition reducing part of Ouster's future sales expansion from 2027. Existing run-rate sales are protected in the scenario, and manufacturing and support cost savings offset part of the revenue loss. No Ouster lost order has been announced.

For the four-quarter earnings window beginning in Q4 2027, our estimated operating loss widens from about $48 million to $51 million. That loss window provides no positive operating-earnings valuation ceiling. The later Q1 2030 model ceiling falls about 8% to $45 per share from $49, using the same valuation method. These are research estimates, dependent on substantial sales growth and execution.

Nearer term, our Q3 operating-expense estimate falls from $47 million to about $44 million after checking management's year-over-year guidance. Ouster's next financial results are scheduled for November 3; those results are not included in this review.

Sources: MicroVision and Blue-Band alliance, Ouster second-quarter financial release, RoboSense third-quarter production update.

ASTRA Research

Tobacco research: IQOS strength, Velo growth and Altria's replacement challenge

Posted Oct 21, 2026, 10:36 a.m. EDT

October 20, 2026

New research on Philip Morris, British American Tobacco and Altria highlights how differently the companies are replacing cigarette profits.

Philip Morris has the strongest established smoke-free business through IQOS. Higher revenue and gross profit per equivalent unit can improve its earnings mix. US ZYN faces tougher competition, while production and customer-acquisition costs absorb part of the growth. Our initial Q4 2027 model ceiling is $187 per share, using 15 times GAAP operating profit.

British American Tobacco offers a growing Velo business alongside its cigarette cash flow. Management aims for about £4 billion in modern-oral sales by 2030. Our initial ceiling is $75 per US ADS, using 10 times normalized operating profit after the Canadian settlement adjustment. Promotions, legal market access and the settlement burden remain material risks.

Altria must replace shrinking premium-cigarette and traditional-oral profit. Growing on! sales help, but retained pricing, manufacturing costs and promotion determine the contribution. NJOY's commercial return remains conditional. Our initial ceiling is $74 per share, using 10 times GAAP operating profit.

These are research estimates for the Q4 2027 valuation horizon, based on modeled profit from Q4 2027 through Q3 2028, rather than company price guidance. Philip Morris reports on October 21 and Altria on October 29; those upcoming results are not included.

Sources: Philip Morris second-quarter results, BAT September strategy update, Altria June financial filing.

Applied Optoelectronics AAOI

Tight supplies of optical manufacturing tools could help AIXTRON secure higher prices on eligible new orders. Our revised model includes a small probability-weighted benefit after delivery, depreciation and support costs.

Microsoft MSFT
